articles.title: Iran says it ‘has no plans to negotiate with US’ despite Trump claims – US politics live
articles.summary:
Trump had told Axios he expected talks to resume a day after he rejected Iran’s proposal to reopen the strait of Hormuz

Hello and welcome to the US politics live blog.

State…

blocks.text: Key events

items: 6m agoIran has 'no plans to negotiate with US' despite Trump claims in media

blocks.text: Iran has 'no plans to negotiate with US' despite Trump claims in media
Hello and welcome to the US politics live blog.
State media in Iran has reported that Iran’s delegation to the UN General Assembly had no talks planned with the United States, after US president Donald Trump said he expected more negotiations.
“Iran’s delegation in New York has no plans for negotiations with the United States,” said the official IRNA news agency, citing an unnamed source close to the group.
Trump told media outlet Axios on Sunday that he expected talks to resume soon, a day after he rejected a proposal by Tehran to reopen the strait of Hormuz within seven days.
“Iran’s views and positions were conveyed clearly and explicitly to the US side... via a Qatari mediator,” IRNA said, adding that the Iranian delegation would return to Tehran on Tuesday.
Iran says it presented seven conditions for ending the war and reopening the strait of Hormuz, a strategic waterway through which roughly 20% of the world’s oil and gas flowed before the war.

The strait lies at the heart of the conflict that began with US-Israeli strikes on Iran in February. Following that attack, Tehran placed a chokehold on the waterway, and Washington responded with a blockade of Iranian ports.

Axios said indirect talks mediated by Qatar could take place as early as today, less than a week after similar discussions between US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner and Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi.
Iran demands a seven-day ceasefire across the Middle East, including in Lebanon, where its ally Hezbollah is regularly bombarded by Israel.
It also demands the unfreezing of its foreign assets, lifting sanctions on its oil sector, and an end to the US naval blockade. Trump rejected their demands on Saturday.
In other developments:

items: The Trump administration on Monday plans to release new fuel economy standards that would relax regulatory requirements for automakers to control pollution from gasoline-powered cars and light trucks. President Donald Trump said on his Truth Social media account on Saturday that the less stringent mileage requirements would “take the waste out of building cars in America” and save families “thousands on a new, beautiful and safe car,” while boosting auto production in the US.

Donald Trump’s attorney general Todd Blanche argued on Sunday that the administration was permitted to ban three news outlets from the White House because “it is a privilege and not a right to be there”. Appearing on the ABC News program This Week during the second week of the White House’s dispute over press credentialing and access, Blanche also said that the administration took the decision to ban CNN, MS Now and Politico beginning on 19 September because the president was “sick and tired” of what he considered to be those media outlets’ inaccurate reporting.

US senator Thom Tillis on Sunday criticized Donald Trump, his fellow Republican, for the president’s support of Ken Paxton over incumbent John Cornyn in the Texas Senate Republican primary. “He made a colossal mistake,” Tillis, a frequent Trump critic from North Carolina, said during an interview on CNN’s State of the Union in reference to the president’s support of Paxton who defeated Cornyn in the May primary.

The United States and China released Monday reciprocal lists of products worth about $30bn each that will see tariff cuts, in a deal expected to boost bilateral trade. The details came days after Chinese President Xi Jinping met with president Donald Trump in Washington in his first state visit to the US since 2015.

Trump justified the pending US arms sale to Taiwan to Chinese president Xi Jinping by downplaying it as just one of many sales Washington makes around the world - even asking Xi if he’d be in the market for US arms, Trump’s ambassador to China said on Sunday.

House Democrats are preparing a vast oversight agenda, with investigations of Trump, his family and his administration if the party sweeps control of the chamber from Republicans in the November elections. The undertaking is as robust as it is daunting, spanning several House committees.

blocks.text: September 28, 2026 | 6:23pm
This photo taken on April 14, 2026 shows a motorist passing by a "price rollback" banner in a gas station along Katipunan Avenue, Quezon City.
The STAR / Miguel De Guzman
MANILA, Philippines — Local pump prices are set to decline this week, ending September with lower fuel costs for motorists and the transport sector after three consecutive weeks of increases.
The Department of Energy said Monday, September 28, that the following price adjustments will take effect starting 6 a.m. Tuesday, September 29:

items: Diesel: down P7.57 per liter
Kerosene: down P5.85 per liter
Gasoline: down P0.24 per liter

blocks.text: The adjustments will remain in effect until Monday, October 5.

The rollback follows three straight weeks of price hikes across major petroleum products, which pushed some pump prices above P100 per liter. Pump prices had climbed sharply this month, with diesel rising by a cumulative P18.31 per liter, kerosene by P16.67 and gasoline by P15.25, according to DOE figures.
DOE Oil Industry Management Bureau Director Rino Abad said last week that global oil prices eased after Saudi Arabia announced that 40% of its oil export operations would resume.
Higher fares for jeepneys and other public utility vehicles took effect on September 28, while transport groups also mounted strikes to demand relief from rising fuel costs.

articles.title: Romualdez files bail petition in P7.44-B plunder case
articles.summary: The Leyte congressman has been detained since September 14 due to his plunder case related to the flood control mess

blocks.text: ROMUALDEZ. File photo of former speaker Martin Romualdez.
Aaron Favila/AP/Sandiganbayan pool
The Leyte congressman has been detained since September 14 due to his plunder case related to the flood control mess

MANILA, Philippines – Leyte 1st District Representative and former House speaker Martin Romualdez filed a petition for bail with the Sandiganbayan 3rd Division on Monday, September 28, for his plunder case.

“Wherefore, premises considered, accused Ferdinand Martin Gomez Romualdez respectfully prays that this Honorable Court: Set the instant Petition for Bail for hearing, at which the Prosecution shall be required to present its evidence to show that the evidence of guilt against accused Ferdinand Martin Gomez Romualdez is strong, and accused Romualdez shall be afforded the opportunity to controvert the same,” said Romualdez’s petition.
Romualdez, cousin of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., is facing a plunder charge before the anti-graft court Sandiganbayan.
The Office of the Ombudsman alleged that Romualdez allegedly acquired ill-gotten wealth amounting to P7.44-billion from kickbacks from flood control and other infrastructure projects.
He was arrested on September 7, but was only detained in the New Quezon City Jail in Payatas, Quezon City, on September 14, after spending a week in two different hospitals.
In his petition, Romualdez argued that there is no proof that he allegedly committed or joined the alleged criminal acts under Section 1(d)(2) or Section 1(d)(6) of the plunder law.

He also said that the testimony of state witnesses and former Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) officials Roberto Bernardo and Henry Alcantara may describe alleged dealings of his co-accused Zaldy Co with DPWH officials and contractors, but not proof of his alleged participation or knowledge in the alleged kickback scheme.
“The recantations and the contradicting affidavits materially weaken the delivery evidence on which the alleged series principally depends,” Romualdez added.

There have been recantations of testimony in Romualdez’s case, including that of former Marine Orly Guteza in August. Guteza alleged that that he was coerced by Senator Rodante Marcoleta and former lawmaker Mike Defensor to falsely implicate Romualdez in the alleged kickback scheme.
Despite these recantations, the Ombudsman believes that their case against Romualdez is still strong.
For grave offenses like plunder, bail is not automatic. An accused like Romualdez needs to file a petition for bail before the court.

The tribunal will hold hearings where the prosecution will present evidence to establish that the evidence of guilt is strong against the accused. The purpose of presentation is not yet to prove that the accused is guilty, but rather if the accused deserves to be allowed to post bail while the trial is ongoing.
If the the court rules that the evidence of guilt is strong, then the petition for bail will be denied. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Will Sara Duterte’s defense recalibrate its strategy mid-trial?
articles.summary: Senator-judge Ping Lacson says the defense's strategy of nitpicking and being too technical may not be working

blocks.text: VEEP. Vice President Sara Duterte arrives at the Quezon City Regional Trial Court, following the issuance of an arrest warrant against her for grave threats, on September 5, 2026.
Jire Carreon/Rappler
Senator-judge Ping Lacson says the defense's strategy of nitpicking and being too technical may not be working

items: Senator-judge Panfilo Lacson advised the defense team in Vice President Sara Duterte's impeachment trial to adjust their overly technical strategy, suggesting it may not be effective.
The defense is examining evidence related to Duterte's alleged unexplained wealth, focusing on contracts secured by Gencorp, which is linked to the Vice President.
Defense spokesperson Michael Poa acknowledged Lacson's comments as constructive criticism and expressed willingness to adjust their strategy to better resonate with the senator-judges.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

On the 30th day of Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial, a senator-judge gave a piece of advice to the defense team. At least for Senator-judge Panfilo “Ping” Lacson, the defense lawyers’ strategy of being “too technical” may not be working.

“Hindi po ito, let me clarify ‘no and emphasize, na hindi po ito prejudgment. Ang hangad ko lang po is baka pwede mag-adjust kayo ng inyong defense strategy kasi I can speak for myself. Pagdating sa masyadong technical at ‘yong impression na nagsisilip lang ng napakaliit na butas, mukhang hindi po nagre-register,” Lacson said during the trial on Monday, September 28.

(This is not, let me clarify, that this is not a prejudgment. What I want is maybe the defense can adjust its strategy because I can speak for myself. The overly technical and the impression that the defense is nitpicking, maybe these strategies are not registering.)

Lacson said this in the middle of the prosecution’s presentation of evidence in relation to Duterte’s alleged unexplained wealth. This would be the third and last article of impeachment of the prosecution if it pushes through with dropping the article on bribery.

On Monday, it was the defense’s turn to examine Philippine Government Electronic Procurement System (PhilGEPS) Division Chief Rendell Sopeña, the prosecution’s witness who testified about the contracts secured by Gencorp.

A Rappler investigation revealed that Gencorp, allegedly linked to the Vice President, cornered P15 million in food and catering contracts from Davao City Hall and PhilHealth between 2022 and 2025. The Dutertes have been ruling Davao City for almost 40 years. (READ: The Dutertes’ 40-year reign: Forged from strongman and victim)

blocks.caption: Sara Duterte’s company won millions’ worth of contracts from Davao City Hall

blocks.text: Through his cross-examination, defense lawyer Roberto Batungbacal highlighted that Gencorp’s contracts went through the regular procurement process. He also said that of the 49 contracts secured by the company, only 15 were awarded by Davao City Hall.

Thirty-three of the contracts were with the Philippine Health Insurance Corporation, while the other one was awarded by Overseas Workers Welfare Administration–Davao Region. Batungbacal also reiterated that these government agencies are independent from Davao City Hall.

The defense lawyer also poked holes into Sopeña’s points by highlighting that the latter’s testimony is limited to the authentication of PhilGEPS documents. Batungbacal, through Sopeña, also noted that irregularities in contracts, if there are any, can only determined by the Commission on Audit, and not by PhilGEPS.

“The way probably and probably some of the non-lawyers among the senator-judges, particularly my seat mate Senator [Lito] Lapid, understand the questions posited by the defense counsel is that the objective of the cross was to create an iota of doubt, no matter how technical and small, to create the impression that the threshold of establishing guilt is beyond reasonable doubt which I believe is not the case in this impeachment trial,” said Lacson.

Apart from creating doubts on the testimony of prosecution witnesses, raising numerous objections also seem to be part of the defense strategy. The defense has repeatedly denied this, saying that they object to questions of the prosecution only if there’s basis for it.

There are also observations that probably, the defense allegedly makes the proceedings boring so that the public will lose interest in the case. But just like in the allegation related to raising too many objections, the defense has also denied this claim and said that this was not their strategy.
But does the defense share the same stance that their strategies may not be working? Will they take Lacson’s friendly advice?

Defense spokesperson and counsel Michael Poa said their lawyers are particular with details due to their experience in trial court litigation. But he said they appreciate comments like Lacson’s and view them as constructive criticism.
He said such comments are helpful to them as they defend the respondent, the Vice President, in the impeachment trial.

“We can also tweak, recalibrate, and better present our side kung ‘yon ang mas maka-register on the side. Kasi ang importante naman dito, senator-judges talaga, ‘di ba? Sila ‘yong mag-ano, nagdedesisyon,” Poa told reporters.
“We’ll just discuss this and see if there’s any way to maybe have some tweaks here and there para lang tumalab,” he added.

(We can also tweak, recalibrate, and better present our side if that will help us register our points on the side. Because the senator-judges are important here, right? They will decide on the case. We’ll just discuss this and see if there’s any way to maybe have some tweaks here and there so our points will register.) – Rappler.com

articles.title: Was police official’s testimony on Sara Duterte’s firearms a ‘waste of time’?
articles.summary: On Day 30 of the impeachment trial, a senator-judge questions the relevance of a police official’s testimony on the firearms owned by Duterte and her husband, Mans Carpio, to the unexplained wealth…

blocks.text: Did the House prosecution panel waste the Senate impeachment court’s time during the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte?

On Day 30 of the impeachment trial, a senator-judge questioned the relevance of a police official’s testimony on the firearms owned by Duterte and her husband, Manases Carpio, to the allegations of unexplained wealth against the Vice President.

Senator-judge Raffy Tulfo said the testimony of Police Major Joericson Sangalang of the Philippine National Police Firearms and Explosives Office (PNP-FEO) was a “waste of time,” arguing that firearms are assets that could be declared as personal property in Statements of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth (SALNs).
Tulfo also said he had made a sample computation of the value of Duterte’s firearms and found that the total remained well within her declared net worth.

“Sorry, but for me, this is a waste of time. We could have done a lot more things than presenting the witness. We could have called for session and passed more bills. For me, this witness is irrelevant to the allegations,” said Tulfo.
Sangalang was called to testify on official PNP-FEO records on the firearms registered to Duterte and Carpio.
Other senator-judges, including Juan Miguel “Migz” Zubiri, expressed similar concern, saying he believes Duterte did not commit any violation if the firearms were properly declared in her SALN.
Presiding officer Francis “Chiz” Escudero allowed the House prosecution panel to proceed with its direct examination.

In his testimony, Sangalang said the couple owned 51 firearms with a combined value of around P7.2 million based on current market prices. These included high-powered pistols, rifles, and shotguns, some worth more than P100,000 each.
In 2024, Rappler reported that the Duterte family owned 654 firearms, 28 of which were registered to the Vice President.

“We were objecting on its relevance. That has always been our position…which was also, I guess, voiced out by some of our senator-judges,” defense counsel Michael Poa said in a mix of English and Filipino.

“But, you know, the PNP-FEO officer was still allowed to present, so we will leave it up to the senator-judges how they will assess the presentation, specifically the market value, because for us, it was irrelevant,” Poa said.

Section 34 of the 2025 Omnibus Rules on the SALN requires the individual declaration of registered personal property, including motor vehicles, boats, aircraft, and firearms. Defense counsel Carlo Joaquin Narvasa, however, argued the provision only applies to 2026 SALNs onwards.

The exchange prompted Tulfo to call for a review of the country’s gun ownership laws, particularly the absence of a limit on the firearms a person may legally own. He also urged government personnel to itemize the declaration of their firearms in SALNs.
“I did not know that a private citizen may own as many firearms that they can…. Perhaps, this is something that lawmakers may revisit,” Tulfo said.
“Maybe we can put a limit on this, otherwise, a person may buy and create an armory. He may also hire goods and use them during elections to establish a private army,” he said.

Zubiri agreed that the law could be revisited but clarified that private armies typically use unlicensed firearms. He also said the existing gun ownership law is “sufficient,” although legislators could consider stricter provisions on the safekeeping of firearms in light of recent school shootings.
“Let’s amend the law to make it stricter on the safekeeping of the firearms,” Zubiri said.

The prosecution, for its part, defended the presentation of Sangalang as a witness. Private prosecutor Lorna Kapunan said in an interview with Rappler that the issue is not the P7-million value of the firearms but a possible pattern of undeclared assets. This, the prosecution said, is relevant to the unexplained wealth allegation against the Vice President.

articles.title: Gracioso dismissal no reason to disregard statements, says NBI chief
articles.summary: Photos and documents submitted by the former policeman will be examined.

blocks.text: September 28, 2026 | 6:14pm
NBI Director Melvin Matibag speaks at a press conference on Monday, May 4, 2026, where he says the now-viral recording was a conversation with his friend in 2020.
The STAR / Edd Gumban

MANILA, Philippines — The dismissal of former policeman Rodulfo Gracioso from the service does not automatically discredit his allegations, although his statements and evidence will face scrutiny, National Bureau of Investigation Director Melvin Matibag said.
In an interview with reporters on Monday, September 28, Matibag said Gracioso's dismissal does not mean the NBI should disregard his statements.
"Just because you were dismissed over a case does not mean we can no longer consider and investigate your statement," Matibag said in Filipino.
Matibag noted that witnesses who face cases or have been dismissed from service may still provide information to ongoing investigations.
He said, however, that Gracioso could face a perjury complaint if his statements are proven false.
The NBI will also authenticate the photos and other documents Gracioso submitted as evidence, Matibag said.
Cash delivery allegations
Personalities named in Gracioso's affidavit, including Vice President Sara Duterte, will also be invited to participate in the fact-finding investigation.

Gracioso, who said he previously served as a security aide of former House speaker Lord Allan Velasco, claimed that he helped deliver suitcases filled with large amounts of cash to Duterte, her brother and former President Rodrigo Duterte.
He alleged making more than 20 deliveries of cash-filled suitcases totaling more than P2 billion to the Vice President and P1 billion to the former president.
Both Vice President Duterte and Velasco have denied Gracioso's allegations.
Philippine National Police chief Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr. confirmed that Gracioso previously served as a security aide of Velasco and was later dismissed over an administrative case.

"Gracioso had been investigated [in an] administrative case and there is a corresponding criminal case filed against him but that was long before. I think it's a case in year 2022 or 2021," Nartatez said.

"The administrative case was eventually resolved, resulting in his dismissal from the service, and before that he also had a suspension that was deemed served," he added, speaking in Filipino and English.
Gracioso submitted to the NBI on Monday the evidence he has to support his allegations against Duterte and Velasco.

articles.title: Larissa Waters steps down as Greens leader due to ill health
articles.summary:
Ballot for new leader expected next week after Waters quits to manage pre-existing kidney disease that has ‘declined significantly’

  • Get our

blocks.text: Greens leader Larissa Waters has announced she will step down due to ill health, with a party room meeting scheduled for next week to choose her successor.
Waters revealed on Monday night she has been managing a pre-existing kidney disease, but that her health had “declined significantly over the course of recent months”.
She said while her prognosis for recovery was positive, the pressure of the party’s leadership, including additional travel demands, was detracting from a focus on her health.
Waters replaced Adam Bandt as Greens leader after the 2025 election, in which Bandt lost his lower house seat in a shock result.
But some Greens members have expressed frustration with the party’s position under Waters, including its cut-through with voters as the major parties haemorrhage support to One Nation.

items: Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

blocks.text: Waters said in a statement she would take a period of medical leave, before returning to parliament to represent Queensland in the Senate.
“It has been a tremendous honour to be leader of the Greens, fighting for people and the planet,” she said.
“I’m really sad that illness means my time as leader has been cut short, but our movement needs a leader in good health to lead us to success at the next election.

“Passing the torch on to the next leader of the party will put them in the best position to take the Greens to the next election, fighting for people, not the corporate interests that run Labor, Liberals and One Nation.
after newsletter promotion
“Our fight is too important, and it needs more time and energy than I am able to give while I focus on my recovery.”

She thanked her colleagues and doctors for their support, citing successes including negotiations with Labor on environmental law reforms and tougher gun laws introduced after last year’s Bondi Beach terror attack.
“I will keep working for the people of Queensland, for women’s safety and for climate action when I am able to return to parliament.”
Deputy leader Mehreen Faruqi, and high profile senators Sarah Hanson-Young, David Shoebridge and Nick McKim could contest the leadership ballot.
Waters was first elected to the Senate in 2011 but was forced to resign in July 2017 after discovering she held duel Canadian citizenship during parliament’s eligibility crisis.
After renouncing her citizenship, she returned to the upper house in September 2018 to fill a vacancy.
Waters was a co-deputy leader to Bandt, and to former leader Richard Di Natale at various times between 2015 and 2022.

As the party’s spokesperson for women, Waters played a role in shaping the independent parliamentary workplace watchdog based on recommendations from Kate Jenkins’ report into the culture in Parliament House.

The Greens have been reduced to a single lower house MP – Ryan’s Elizabeth Watson-Brown – after the May election, with minor primary vote swings against Bandt and two Queensland incumbents, Max Chandler-Mather and Stephen Bates.
The party maintains the losses were due to a drop in votes for the Liberal party favouring Labor candidates, as well as a reduction in favourable preference flows.

articles.title: Disgraced former Manitoba law dean racked up millions in Swiss debt ahead of France arrest, documents suggest
articles.summary: The elusive former head of Manitoba's lone law school — who'd been in the wind since being disbarred 2½ years ago — racked up millions in debt in Switzerland before he was recently picked up by…

image.caption: Jonathan Black-Branch disappeared from Canada before he was disbarred by the Law Society of Manitoba in 2024. He was arrested in France recently and faces extradition. (University of Manitoba)

blocks.text: Manitoba·New

The elusive former head of Manitoba's lone law school — who'd been in the wind since being disbarred 2½ years ago — racked up millions in debt in Switzerland before he was recently picked up by police in France.
Public records indicate Jonathan Black-Branch owes over $5M, mostly to banks

Jonathan Black-Branch owes the equivalent of $5.67 million to Swiss banks, in municipal taxes, mortgage payments and an art gallery, among other parties, according to public Swiss government financial documents reviewed by CBC News.
"We can only guess why individuals engage in this type of behaviour," said Christian Leuprecht, security expert and co-editor of the book Dirty Money: Financial Crime in Canada.
"But clearly this is somebody who understood contract law, corporate law and how to weaponize that against the people who lent him money and also how to obfuscate processes."

Black-Branch, the former University of Manitoba law school dean, was recently arrested in France, years after disappearing from his post and failing to appear at his professional misconduct hearings, which revealed hundreds of thousands of dollars in misappropriated funds from the university.
A search of "Jonathan Lee Black-Branch" in the Swiss government's official Gazette generates at least 22 hits detailing debts and orders to pay in 2025 and 2026.
The debts total 3.29 million Swiss francs, or $5.62 million, according to Bank of Canada exchange rates as of Thursday.

items: Suspicions around former U of Manitoba law school dean's expenses surfaced in 2019, hearing told
Ethics expert slams U of Manitoba for lack of legal action against law dean accused of misspending

blocks.text: Some of those public debt records suggest Black-Branch owed $71,700 to a Zurich-based art gallery.

Five other records suggest he owed over $30,000 in state and municipal taxes to the canton of Thurgau, a jurisdiction in the northeast of Switzerland. Some of those taxes go back to 2023, according to Swiss records.

The majority of the Swiss debt — $5.43 million Cdn — is tied up in real estate agreements, including mortgage payments owed, to Thurgauer Kantonalbank in Switzerland, records suggest. One such entry — dated March 3, 2026 — includes a note describing Black-Branch as "currently of unknown whereabouts."
He vacated his position as dean of the University of Manitoba law school suddenly in 2020.
Black-Branch disappeared amid drawn-out professional misconduct proceedings in Winnipeg that ultimately led to his disbarment by the Law Society of Manitoba in early 2024.
The law society found he misappropriated over $600,000 from the U of M and an endowment fund while dean of the law school from 2016-2020.

Black-Branch misspent that on expensive meals at a Winnipeg board game restaurant and at the private-members' Manitoba Club, as well as on travel and his own professional development coursework at schools such as Yale and Harvard.
Though reluctant to pursue criminal charges initially, the U of M asked Winnipeg police to investigate in late 2023, shortly before Black-Branch's disbarment. His whereabouts were unknown by then.
Black-Branch, 64, was subsequently disbarred in the United Kingdom and Wales last year and fined nearly $5,000.
A Canada-wide warrant had been in effect since earlier this year, ahead of Black-Branch's recent arrest.

items: Former law dean charged dozens of meals with 3 lawyers to U of Manitoba. They say meals never happened
Former Manitoba law school dean can't be trusted as lawyer and should be disbarred, law society lawyer says

blocks.text: Extradition processes have begun, but it's too soon to say whether that will necessarily lead to him being sent back to Canada soon, or at all.

"France certainly isn't a country that is reluctant to extradite, it is just there are many checks and balances," said Gaspard Lindon, an attorney with the Paris Bar Association, where he practises criminal law and general litigation.
If someone were to consent to extradition, that could expedite things, he said.
Lindon, who isn't involved in Black-Branch's case, suggested that from what he understands of the case, Black-Branch might be less likely to do that.

"If you've been caught in a foreign country, and you're contemplating spending weeks and months … potentially in a foreign cell, it makes a lot of sense sometimes to consent to being extradited," he said. "But then, if you're litigating and not consenting to extradition, then it can take weeks, months. It all depends."

Leuprecht, a professor at the Royal Military College of Canada, said the lack of co-ordination between North American and European credit rating agencies can create an opening for someone with the legal and financial know-how to exploit financial institutions.

"You find yourself a new financial institution, and you show up with enough money to get yourself started. You're probably able to convince people that you're worthy of credit," said Leuprecht, noting one area of expertise Black-Branch has is corporate law.
"This seems to be a case of somebody who's turned his professional knowledge against his own profession."

Leuprecht said his work on financial crime suggests there are a few key "professional enablers" — accountants, lawyers, real estate agents and others — who are "essential to making illicit financial flows work, especially at scale."
Lawyers play a particularly important role in global financial crime, Leuprecht said, because of how they might set up corporate structures to reroute money illicitly.
"It's one thing to get him extradited. It'll be a very different matter of actually trying to recover any of the funds," he said.

articles.title: Plan for controversial $1.2bn datacentre in Sydney scrapped due to ‘emerging’ regulations
articles.summary:
Developer Goodman Group says changes in government rules are behind decision to pull plug on ‘Project Mars’ in Lane Cove

  • Get our

blocks.text: Plans for a controversial $1.2bn datacentre in Lane Cove in Sydney’s north have been withdrawn, with the developer blaming “emerging” regulations from the state and federal governments for the decision to pull the plug.

The “Project Mars” plans were withdrawn from the NSW planning portal on Monday, with the developer, Goodman Group, posting on its site that the policy and regulatory environment for large-scale datacentres had “evolved significantly”.
“Having considered emerging federal and state policy, Goodman has concluded that it will not progress with the development application.”

In August, the NSW government announced its new “fast-track” framework for datacentre applications that promised to assess applications within 75 days if the plans meet set principles, including applying “world-class” standards for noise and air pollution, imposing no net cost to consumers and communities and funding additional water and energy supply.

It followed the federal government’s rules in July aimed at addressing growing community concerns with datacentre location choices, and energy and water use requirements, with legislation expected to hit the federal parliament early next year.
The Lane Cove proposal had become one of the main sources of criticism of the datacentre growth in Australia.

The proposal had been criticised by local residents due to its proximity to local schools, event spaces and green space, as well as the growing concerns about clustering with a number of datacentres planned or in operation in Lane Cove. Guardian Australia first reported the community concerns in May.
Lane Cove Responsible planning spokesperson Sasha Titchkosky said she was “absolutely ecstatic” at the decision to withdraw the plans.
after newsletter promotion

“I think we could have all saved everyone a lot of hassle and heartache if we actually had an appropriate regulatory regime and the government at state and federal had jumped on this when we started calling for better regulation.
“There was a real regulatory gap and that’s causing issues all around the country with inappropriate datacentres being put forward that really don’t give communities any benefits.”
Titchkosky thanked Goodman Group for listening to community concern and withdrawing the proposal.

A spokesperson for Goodman Group declined to comment further, but pointed to the opening statement made by the company’s general manager for development, Ben McGilp, at last week’s hearing of the Senate inquiry into datacentres.
McGilp said the company supports “clear, consistent and evidence-based regulation that provides confidence for communities, governments and industry”.
The peak body for the sector, Data Centres Australia, warned the committee in its submission to the inquiry that the risk for Australia is not over-building datacentres but “under-building”.

“Turning the investment away does not reduce global data centre energy or water use, it simply redirects it to jurisdictions with weaker protections than Australia’s, while Australia forgoes the economic value and the sovereign capability.”

articles.title: PCG: Chinese ship faked location near Batanes cable corridor
articles.summary: The Chinese survey ship hid movements off Batanes, the Philippine Coast Guard says.

blocks.text: September 28, 2026 | 5:53pm

The Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) has confirmed the presence of the Chinese research vessel (CRV) JIA HAI KE 7 approximately 37.84 nautical miles northwest of Itbayat, Batanes, within the Philippine exclusive economic zone (EEZ), Sept. 28, 2026.
Philippine Coast Guard
MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine Coast Guard has accused a Chinese ship of deliberately broadcasting a false location to hide its movements in the waters off Batanes.
The Chinese ship, Jia Hai Ke 7, had been holding its position in waters crossed by undersea cables, which the PCG said was consistent with an unauthorized seabed survey.

"A seabed-survey vessel hiding its position while holding station in this corridor raises serious concern over the security of the country's undersea communications infrastructure and the potential military use of the data collected," the PCG said in a statement.

The PCG checked the ship's movements using Canada's Dark Vessel Detection system. The ship's Automatic Identification System, the transponder that broadcasts a vessel's identity and position, showed it leaving Xiamen in China's Fujian province past midnight on September 21.
By 8:10 p.m. that day, its signal placed it somewhere off Bindari, Papua New Guinea, more than 2,000 nautical miles away.
The PCG called the trail "physically impossible" and said the ship falsified its location to hide its movements from Philippine authorities.

A PCG monitoring station in Itbayat detected the ship. On Monday morning, a patrol plane sent by Admiral Ronnie Gil Gavan, the coast guard commandant, confirmed it was about 38 nautical miles northwest of Itbayat, inside the Philippines' exclusive economic zone.
Itbayat is the country's northernmost municipality and is around 160 kilometers from Taiwan.
The PCG said its aircraft crew radioed the Chinese ship several times to explain its presence and stop any unauthorized activity. The ship did not respond.

Batanes sits between northern Luzon and Taiwan, which Beijing claims as its territory. In June, Chinese scholars argued that Batanes is a natural extension of Taiwan, a claim vehemently rejected by the Philippine government.

This comes days after Chinese navy and coast guard ships interfered with a Philippine resupply mission to Ayungin Shoal on September 24, an incident the United States condemned on Sunday, September 27.

articles.title: Marcos calls Sara Duterte a ‘liar’ for linking Gracioso claims to admin
articles.summary: Marcos chose to respond to Duterte this time as her accusations became repetitive, Claire Castro said.

blocks.text: September 28, 2026 | 5:47pm

MANILA, Philippines — President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. called Vice President Sara Duterte a "liar" after she accused his administration of using a former policeman's cash delivery allegations to undermine her.

At a Palace briefing on Monday, September 28, Press Officer Claire Castro said Marcos personally called her to relay his response to Duterte's statement about dismissed police patrolman Rodulfo Gracioso Jr.

"Ito po mismo ay mensahe ng pangulo patungkol sa komento na 'yan ng Bise Presidente. Ang sabi po niya: 'Yan po ay nonsense, fake news, mahihilig magsinungaling. Mga buwaon. Ulitin natin, mga buwaon. Translate natin: sinungaling," Castro said.
("This is the president's message regarding the vice president's comment. He said: 'That is nonsense, fake news. They like to lie. Liars.' Again, liars.")
'Desperation'

On Saturday, September 26, Duterte issued a statement denying that she knew Gracioso or received money from him, calling his allegations "another media stunt" meant to prop up what she described as a "faltering impeachment case."
"The desperation of the administration to bring me down, push for Charter Change, prevent the 2028 elections, and cling to power is becoming increasingly diabolical," Duterte said.

Her statement came after Gracioso alleged that he had delivered cash-filled suitcases to Duterte, former President Rodrigo Duterte and Davao City 1st District Rep. Paolo "Pulong" Duterte on the instructions of former House Speaker Lord Allan Velasco.

Gracioso claimed he made more than 20 cash deliveries to the vice president totaling more than P2 billion. The allegations are being investigated by the National Bureau of Investigation and have not been independently established as fact.

Earlier Monday, Philippine National Police chief Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr. confirmed that Gracioso had been assigned as part of Velasco's security detail. PNP records also show that Gracioso had been demoted from police corporal to patrolman before his dismissal from the service this month.
Velasco's camp has denied Gracioso's allegations, describing them as fabricated and inconsistent with verifiable events.
'Repetitive' accusations
Castro said Marcos chose to respond more directly this time because Duterte's accusations against him and his administration had become repetitive.
"Paulit-ulit po kasi. Paulit-ulit, hindi tumitigil sa paninira kay pangulo, sa paninira sa administrasyong ito," Castro said.
("It is repetitive. The attacks against the president and this administration do not stop.")
"So hindi po puwedeng isabalewala na lang ang lahat ng mga kasinungalingang ito na namumutawi sa isang obstructionist, sa isang destabilizer," she added.
("So we cannot simply disregard all these lies coming from an obstructionist, from a destabilizer.")
Asked how seriously the Palace views Gracioso's allegations, Castro said they should be investigated if he can substantiate them with evidence.
"Kung mapapatunayan naman po ni Mr. Gracioso 'yung kanyang mga isiniwalat at kung may mga ebidensya naman po siyang maipapakita, dapat lang pong seryosohin ang pag-iimbestiga dito," Castro said.
("If Mr. Gracioso can prove what he has disclosed and can present evidence, then this should be seriously investigated.")

articles.title: Will Jürgen Klopp's charisma be enough for Germany?
articles.summary: After defeat to Greece, Jürgen Klopp is confronted with the real challenge of his task as Germany head coach. Can his charisma alone push this group forward?

image.caption: Jürgen Klopp has a lot of work to do, but is his charisma alone enough to carry this Germany team?Image: Steffie Wunderl/BEAUTIFUL SPORTS/picture alliance

blocks.text: In his first season in charge at Liverpool, Jürgen Klopp lost just one of his first five games. Germany are hoping for a similar run emerges after a shock defeat to Greece left Klopp with just one point after his first two games.
Klopp's response was familiar. The head coach took responsibility for the loss, shielding this new crop of Germany players from criticism.
"We have been together for a week now, all mixed together, and that needs time," Klopp said after the match.

"Let the new players develop. The established players are top players at their clubs, and they have my support. Feel free to criticize me, but not the boys. We don't need to completely tear everything apart. I was surprised that some people booed. The future is as bright as we make it. We'll take it on with everything we have."
He also emphasized development over short-term panic, citing the need for more training sessions to cement the automatic responses needed to break down well-organized defenses.
International coaching is different

Herein lies the challenge for one of football's greatest coaches. In likely his final job as a head coach, can the multiple league winner adapt his coaching methods to work in the international setting? Klopp, a coach and a person famous for his ability to develop relationships and grow a team at a club, has said he believes he can adapt.

There is no doubt his communication style is what this team needs. His charismatic focus on developing a culture and growing collectively in connection with the fans is what is required. And after many years of frustration and pain watching Germany's men at major tournaments, the biggest mistake would be to tear down this new group before it even begins.

It both needs and deserves the time to figure out how far it can go. Bambase Conte and Hennes Behrens made their debuts vs. Greece after a host of others had done so against the Netherlands. These are the first steps towards finding out who will drive Germany towards an improved outing at Euro 2028 in two summer's time. It is the main reason why Klopp chose so many players for these first four games.
Can Klopp alone compensate should ability be lacking?

But what if, for all of Klopp's positivity and culture building, this new generation of Germany players is just not good enough to win a trophy? Clearly, it is too soon to know the answer to that question, as Klopp himself has said.
"We want to help prepare these players to be competing at the very top over the next two or three years," Klopp had said at his unveiling.
"We took a different approach and focused not on what we don't have, but on what we do have."
What Germany do have right now is both a new team looking to grow and a team that just suffered their first-ever defeat to Greece.

At Liverpool, it took Jürgen Klopp two years and approximately 500 odd training sessions, to reach the point where the team looked like his. In the 2017-18 season, they reached the Champions League final. Alongside the time it took for the team to learn the new system, new signings, notably Mo Salah, Roberto Firmino and Sadio Mane, improved the quality.

Klopp doesn't have that option in the Germany job. He has to do more with fewer training sessions – Klopp will have approximately 200 before Euro 2028. And the closest he can get to new signings are by calling up uncapped Germany players – there were 11 first-time call-ups in this Germany squad.
The 59-year-old said his whole career brought him to this job. It might well prove to be the greatest challenge of his career too.

articles.title: SC adopts term 'victim-survivor' in sexual violence cases
articles.summary: The Supreme Court (SC) has adopted the term “victim-survivor” when referring to individuals who have experienced sexual violence, as it affirmed the conviction of a man for raping his 12-year-old…

blocks.text: Published September 28, 2026 5:35pm

The Supreme Court (SC) has adopted the term “victim-survivor” when referring to individuals who have experienced sexual violence, as it affirmed the conviction of a man for raping his 12-year-old stepdaughter.
In a 15-page decision, the SC’s Third Division said the term acknowledges both the harm inflicted on victims and their continuing dignity.
“This deliberate choice of words recognizes the harm and suffering inflicted while affirming the agency, resiliency, and continuing dignity of those who survive such violence,” it said.

According to court records, the man assaulted the victim outside her uncle’s house in 2018 while everyone was asleep. He then pointed a knife at her and threatened to kill her if she reported the assault.
The victim later told her aunt and uncle about the rape and disclosed that her stepfather had been abusing her since she was nine years old.
Both the Regional Trial Court and the Court of Appeals found the man guilty.
The SC affirmed his conviction and sentence of reclusion perpetua, but deleted the phrase “without eligibility for parole.”
It also ordered him to pay the victim-survivor P450,000 in civil indemnity, moral damages and exemplary damages.
The SC also directed the Department of Social Welfare and Development to refer the victim-survivor to the appropriate rape crisis center for necessary assistance.
Such assistance may include psychological counseling, medical and health services, including medico-legal examination, psychological counseling for her family, and programs for her recovery.
The decision, penned by Associate Justice Japar Dimaampao, was promulgated in February 2026 and made public in September 2026.— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Ireland beat Israel 3-0 in Nations League match overshadowed by political controversy
articles.summary: Ireland easily beat Israel in a Nations League fixture that 24 hours earlier appeared in doubt. One Irish player pulled out of the match to express his opposition to Israel's actions in the Gaza…

image.caption: Members of the Irish team bowed their heads during playing of the Israeli national anthemImage: Inpho Photography/IMAGO

blocks.text: The Irish team bowed their heads during playing of the Israeli national anthem on Sunday night and they declined to shake hands with their opponents, a gesture that is customary before international fixtures.

Ireland played the match wearing black armbands in memory of those killed in Israel's military operation in the Gaza Strip, and just 24 hours earlier it was unclear whether the match would go ahead at all.
'Significant majority' vote to play
On Saturday, the players voted in favor of playing what was technically a home match for Israel in Debrecen, Hungary, despite widespread opposition to their participation among the Irish public.

David Courell, the chief executive of the Irish FA (FAI), told a press conference that had been delayed for several hours while players and coaches met to discuss the issue, that a significant majority of the squad had voted to play.
"Based on that, the association took ⁠the decision on behalf of Irish ​football that this fixture would continue, as we have always intended to fulfil the fixtures," he said.
However, the vote was not unanimous and one player, reserve goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu, decided to pull out of the squad for this and a second match against Israel during this international break.
In Sunday's match, Troy Parrott netted the opener for Ireland in the 14th minute, with ​Adam Idah scoring two minutes later. Jack Moylan added a third in the 25th to make the final score 3-0.

blocks.caption: Troy Parrott opened the scoring for IrelandImage: Inpho Photography/IMAGO

blocks.text: Few supporters present
The fixture was played in a largely empty stadium in Debrecen, with just a few hundred Israeli fans and a handful of Irish supporters in attendance.
The FAI had not reserved any tickets for their fans to attend the match and public broadcaster RTE showed the match without the usual halftime analysis.
Over the previous few days, the Irish team had been under intense pressure from Irish fans and politicians to boycott the fixture.

Ireland has long been a strong supporter of the Palestinian cause and formally recognized a Palestinian state in 2024 alongside Spain and Norway. Dublin has also repeatedly criticized Israel over the Gaza conflict.
A Hamas raid into Israel on October 7, 2023, killed around 1,200 people, prompting Israel's attack on Gaza which has killed over 73,000.

Ireland's next Nations League match was originally scheduled to be played in Dublin on October 4, but due to security concerns, it has been moved to the Serbian town of Backa Topola, where it is to be played behind closed doors.

articles.title: Sara Duterte impeachment trial: VP has 22 firearms, says witness
articles.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte owns at least 22 firearms, including a shotgun and five rifles, a prosecution witness said Monday.

blocks.text: Published September 28, 2026 5:25pm
Vice President Sara Duterte owns at least 22 firearms, including a shotgun and five rifles, a prosecution witness said Monday.

Police Major Jerickson Sangalang, Records Division chief of the Philippine National Police Firearms and Explosives Office (PNP-FEO), made the testimony during the Day 30 of the impeachment trial of the Vice President during the direct examination of House prosecutor Belle Zamora of San Juan.
Sangalang said the Vice President has 22 firearms consisting of:

items: 14 pistols
two revolvers
five rifles, of which three are Class A light weapons
one shotgun

blocks.text: “These are worth P2.184 million,” Sangalang said of the worth of the guns based on market survey.
He also said that the Vice President’s husband, lawyer Manases Carpio, owns 29 firearms, including one expired firearm:

items: 16 pistols
two revolvers
one shotgun
10 rifles, of which one is a Class A light weapon

blocks.text: The PNP official said the total worth of Carpio’s firearms is at least P5 million.
Sangalang is one of the witnesses of the prosecution for Article 2 of the Articles of Impeachment which accuses the Vice President of accumulating unexplained wealth through the following:

items: failure to fully and truthfully disclose all her and her spouse's assets, liabilities, and net worth in her statement of assets, liabilities, and net worth (SALN) including in her SALN for the years 2022, 2023, and 2024; and
failure to divest, and instead, willfully continued, all her business interests during her tenure as vice president for the years 2022, 2023, 2024, and 2025.

blocks.text: The prosecution offered Sangalang's testimony to prove:

items: that the respondent Vice President Duterte and her husband possess Licenses to Own and Possess Firearms ("LTOPF") Type 5, and are classified as "Certified Gun Collectors"

that the Vice President and her husband maintain a hobby in gun collecting by owning, possessing, and maintaining more than 50 firearms, which includes pistols, revolvers, rifles, and shotguns with total value of at least P7 million and
to prove other relevant allegations and to identify and authenticate relevant documents

blocks.text: — BM, GMA News

articles.title: PCG files falsification complaint vs. MV June Aster's captain
articles.summary: The Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) has filed a criminal complaint for falsification of documents against the captain of the ill-fated MV June Aster, which went up in flames in a fire that killed 77…

blocks.text: Published September 28, 2026 5:14pm

The Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) has filed a criminal complaint for falsification of documents against the captain of the ill-fated MV June Aster, which went up in flames in a fire that killed 77 people, with eight still missing.
There were 43 survivors.
The complaint was filed before the National Prosecution Service (NPS) of the Department of Justice in Manila on September 23.

PCG spokesperson Commodore Noemie Cayabyab said the complaint stemmed from documents submitted by Sarmiento as part of the vessel's Master's Declaration of Safe Departure (MDSD), which contains the declared number of individuals onboard.
The PCG said other criminal complaints are also being prepared based on evidence gathered during its ongoing investigation.

"During this incident, may anim tayong pasahero na initially nasa ticket manifest na hindi po nakasakay sa barko. So ’yan po ’yung mga tinitingnan po natin. Pangalawa, during the investigation, may mga nakita rin po tayong double entry ng pangalan ng isang pasahero. At ang isa po doon ay may nakalista pong pangalan ng crew at hindi po actual na sumakay," Cayabyab said on Super Radyo dzBB.

"So i-highlight ko lang po... itong MDSD na binabanggit ko po dati. It is the declaration of the captain na ang kanyang barko ay ligtas and seaworthy to sail, declaring as well na itong barko niya is in safe condition, compliant sa lahat ng mga safety rules and regulations, to include po ’yung manning requirement and competency po ng crew na sakay po niya, at of course ’yung kahandaan po niya—ang kahandaan ng barko—before maglayag," she added.

(Regarding this incident, there were six passengers initially listed on the ticket manifest who did not actually board the vessel. That is one of the matters we are looking into. Secondly, during the investigation, we also discovered a duplicate entry for a passenger's name; in one instance, a crew member's name was listed, yet that person did not actually board the ship... I would also like to highlight... the MDSDcis the captain's declaration that his vessel is safe and seaworthy; he declares that the ship is in safe condition and compliant with all safety rules and regulations—including manning requirements and the crew's competence—as well as the vessel's overall readiness before departure.)
Meanwhile, the PCG continues to provide free legal assistance to affected families.
Aerial search operations continue for the eight missing individuals in the waters off Palawan and Southern Tagalog.
Atienza Interisland Ferries Inc. and its hired salvor, C.V. Gaspar Salvage and Lighterage Corp., are also discussing measures to speed up the salvage operation of the MV June Aster.
On September 9, the passenger vessel caught fire in the waters of Coron, Palawan. –NB, GMA News

articles.title: Sweden faces political deadlock after election-winning center-left bloc fails to form government
articles.summary: Swedish Social Democratic Party leader Magdalena Andersson has abandoned efforts to form a four-party government. Deep divisions within the election-winning bloc have left Sweden in political…

image.caption: The collapse of Andersson's government talks gives Sweden's outgoing right-wing bloc a chance to try to remain in powerImage: Jonas Ekströmer/TT NEWS AGENCY/picture alliance

blocks.text: The leader of Sweden's center-left Social Democratic Party, Magdalena Andersson, on Monday said her talks with other parties had failed to form a government after her bloc's narrow election victory.
The breakdown leaves Sweden without a new government more than two weeks after the election and opens the door for the outgoing right-wing bloc to try to remain in power despite losing the vote.
Why did Sweden's government talks fail?
Andersson had been trying to bring together the Social Democrats, Greens, Center Party and Left Party, which together won 176 of parliament's 349 seats.
But talks foundered on deep divisions between the centrist Center Party and socialist Left Party.
"Based on the discussions I have had, I can conclude that, as things currently stand, it is not possible for me to form a government," Andersson told reporters.
The four-party bloc won 176 seats in the September 13 election, compared with 173 for the outgoing right-wing alliance. The popular vote difference was around 50,000.
What happens next?

The speaker of parliament is now expected to ask another party leader to try to form a government, with outgoing Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson of the center-right Moderate Party the likely next choice.
How Sweden's tough migration policy impacts youth

Kristersson continues to lead a caretaker government. His bloc, which includes the far-right Sweden Democrats, has also failed to secure a majority and would probably need support from the Center Party.
Center Party leader Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist has ruled out supporting a government that gives influence to either the Sweden Democrats or the Left Party.
Protracted government formation is not unusual in Sweden. It took 37 days to establish a government following the 2022 election and 134 days after the vote in 2018.

articles.title: After a dead whale washed up at a Perth beach, some took selfies. Others held their nose from the stench
articles.summary:
Local authorities have closed the beach for several kilometres and multiple sharks have been spotted in the area

  • Get our

blocks.text: Multiple sharks have been spotted swimming near a large, smelly whale carcass that has washed ashore at a popular capital city beach, drawing hundreds of onlookers.
Surf lifesavers found the dead animal at Perth’s City beach at about 7.30am on Monday and raised the alarm.
Local authorities closed the beach for several kilometres in each direction of the carcass, which appeared to be about six metres long.
Multiple sharks have been spotted in the area, including a five-metre great white.

“It is possible the carcass will continue to act as an attractant that could lead to sharks coming in close to shore along this stretch of coast,” the Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development warned.
“People should exercise additional caution.”

blocks.caption: The whale was found on Monday morning.  Photograph: Richard Wainwright/AAP

blocks.text: The alerts come 10 days after 63-year-old Greg O’Neill was killed in a shark attack while swimming close to shore at Perth’s Sorrento beach, about 12km north of City beach.
Hundreds of onlookers gathered on Monday to view the whale.
“It’s sad, they’re such a beautiful animal,” a local, David Jones, said. Several dead whales had washed up on the same stretch of coast in the previous decade, he said.
Many onlookers took selfies in front of the massive carcass, while others held their noses to protect themselves from the stench.
The silhouettes of sharks could be seen in the waves, swimming up and down the coast.

blocks.caption: Onlookers gathered at City beach in Perth. Photograph: Aaron Bunch/EPA

blocks.text: Town of Cambridge mayor, Gary Mack, said it was important members of the public took heed of the warnings.
“This is not a time for taking risks,” he said.
Mack said authorities were assessing the carcass and it was likely to be removed from the beach on Tuesday.
“It seems at this stage the plan will be to remove the carcass on the back of a truck and take it to a landfill site,” he said.
The other option is to tow it out to sea, but Mack said that may prove difficult.
“There’s a bit of surf down there, and it’s rocking back and forth and appears to be wedged on the sandbar,” he said.

articles.title: Senate impeachment court issues stern warning on Ridon
articles.summary: The Senate impeachment court issued a stern warning on House prosecutor Terry Ridon of Bicol Saro party-list over his comments on the ongoing impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte.

blocks.text: Published September 28, 2026 5:11pm
The Senate impeachment court issued a stern warning on House prosecutor Terry Ridon of Bicol Saro party-list over his comments on the ongoing impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte.

The court noted that while Rule 18 of the Impeachment rules bans parties from commenting on the merits of the case, Ridon’s comments were made in good faith and ultimately deferred to the senator-judges’ evaluation of the evidence.

“The Court gives due weight to Rep. Ridon's explanation that he acted in good faith and his recognition that the ultimate determination ultimately belongs to the senator-judges. The Court likewise notes Rep. Ridon's assertion that he understands the distinction between reporting what transpired in the proceedings, explaining procedural developments, and commenting on matters that are for the Court's determination,” the Senate court said.
“Accordingly, the Court hereby issues a stern warning to Rep. Terry Ridon to exercise greater restraint in future public statements concerning the merits of the pending impeachment trial,” it added.

The impeachment court also said that while Rule 18 allows parties to inform the public of what occurred in the proceedings, it does not allow evaluation of evidence proves or why it supports a party's position.

“While an impeachment trial involves matters of public concern and the public entitled to be informed of its developments, its nature as both a legal and political proceeding demands greater not lesser restraint from counsel who are bound by the Code of Professional Responsibility and Accountability,” the court said.

“This [decision] is to ensure that any decision made by senator-judges is based not on statements publicized outside the court but upon evidence and arguments presented and tested within its established parameters,” the court added.
In response, Ridon vowed to comply with the court's ruling and thanked it for being gracious.
"We accept the warning, and we thank the Senate impeachment court for their graciousness," Ridon said.

"We are committed to exercise greater strength on particular details of the Impeachment proceedings moving forward, but we will continue on with our work as lead prosecutor for unexplained wealth," Ridon added. — RSJ, GMA News

articles.title: Palace: No cover-up in 'anomalous' Taguig flood control projects
articles.summary: Malacañang on Monday assured the public that there would be no cover-up in the investigation into alleged anomalous flood control projects in Taguig City after Senator Panfilo Lacson questioned the…

blocks.text: Published September 28, 2026 5:09pm

Malacañang on Monday assured the public that there would be no cover-up in the investigation into alleged anomalous flood control projects in Taguig City after Senator Panfilo Lacson questioned the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) over a supposed project in the city whose coordinates were found to be in the Visayas.

Palace Press Officer Undersecretary Claire Castro said President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. had ordered an investigation into the alleged anomalous flood control projects, including any DPWH officials found to be involved in a cover-up.

“Kung meron mang tauhan ang DPWH na nais magtakip, ito po ay isang paalala na ang Pangulo po ang nais ay tamang pag-iimbestiga, sapat na pag-iimbestiga, walang kinakanlong, walang itinatago, lalo lalo na kung ito ay mga kaaliyado,” Castro said in a press briefing.

(If there are any DPWH personnel who intend to cover up anything, this is a reminder that the President wants a proper and thorough investigation, with no one being shielded and nothing being concealed, especially when those involved are allies.)

“Definitely, kailangan (magkakaroon ng sibakan) kung merong hindi magandang nangyayari sa DPWH. Kung may pinagtatakpan na mga kaibigan, kaalyado, hindi magdadalawang-isip ang Pangulo na sibakin ang mga taong gumagawa nito dahil definitely, absolutely, prejudicial ito sa gobyerno,” she added.

(Definitely, there will be dismissals if something improper is happening within the DPWH. If there are people covering up for friends or allies, the President will not hesitate to dismiss those responsible because this is definitely and absolutely prejudicial to the government.)
Castro also said the DPWH was investigating the coordinates flagged by Lacson.
The senator said geotagged photos of the projects attached to billing reports “reflected coordinates located approximately 600 kilometers away in Leyte Province.”
Lacson also claimed that the contractor for the project was linked to the Discaya couple, who have been implicated in the flood control controversy.
The senator's social media post came after DPWH Secretary Vince Dizon said his office had yet to find a ghost or non-existent infrastructure project in Taguig City.

“Ang binabanggit lamang po niya (DPWH Secretary Dizon) dito ay patungkol doon sa mga conclusive na mga ghost projects. So wala daw doon sa sampu na alam niyang conclusive ghost projects yung itinatanong sa kanya,” Castro said.

(What he [DPWH Secretary Dizon] was referring to were projects conclusively identified as ghost projects. He said none of the 10 projects being asked about were among those he knew to have been conclusively identified as ghost projects.)
“Niliwanag niya ito at kinakailangan ng mas masusi at mabusising na imbestigasyon dahil hindi naman kinakailangan na cover up,” she added.
(He clarified this, and a more thorough and comprehensive investigation is needed. There is no need for any cover-up.)
In a separate interview, Dizon denied that the DPWH was focusing its investigation into alleged anomalous flood control projects on any particular area.

“There are almost 200 ongoing investigations all over the country. So hindi pwedeng sabihin na nakatutuok sa lugar ito. Iba’t iba 'yan (so we cannot say we are focusing on only one area. They involve different areas),” Dizon said.
Dizon says DPWH has nearly 200 ongoing flood control investigations
— Mariel Celine Serquiña

A couple of editorial points I changed: “the Discaya couple, who are big figures in the flood control scandal” was softened to “who have been implicated in the flood control controversy” to avoid adopting a potentially loaded characterization as fact. I also changed “will be no cover-up” to “there would be no cover-up in the investigation” for cleaner news style.

articles.title: PCG challenges Chinese research vessel loitering off Batanes
articles.summary: The Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) on Monday challenged a Chinese research vessel that was loitering within the country's exclusive economic zone (EEZ) off Itbayat, Batanes.

blocks.text: Published September 28, 2026 5:00pm
The Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) on Monday challenged a Chinese research vessel that was loitering within the country's exclusive economic zone (EEZ) off Itbayat, Batanes.
In a statement, Rear Admiral Jay Tarriela, PCG spokesperson for the West Philippine Sea, said the Chinese research vessel Jia Hai Ke 7 was spotted about 38 nautical miles northwest of Itbayat.

Tarriela said a PCG aircraft challenged the vessel several times over the radio, asserting the Philippines' sovereign rights and asking the ship to state its intentions and stop any unauthorized activity.
However, the Chinese vessel did not respond to the radio challenges.
"The vessel's behavior is not that of a ship in innocent passage," Tarriela said.
Tarriela said the vessel was initially detected by the PCG monitoring station in Itbayat.
A verification using the Canada-provided Dark Vessel Detection (DVD) system reportedly showed an "impossible" AIS (Automatic Identification System) trail.

According to Tarriela, the Jia Hai Ke 7 reported departing Xiamen, Fujian, at 12:59 a.m. on September 21 and was supposedly transmitting from off Bindari, Papua New Guinea, by 8:10 p.m. the same day, a distance of more than 2,000 nautical miles.
By 6:55 a.m. on Monday, the vessel was transmitting from northwest of Itbayat, he said.
"The PCG assesses this as deliberate AIS spoofing to conceal the vessel's true movements from Philippine authorities," Tarriela said.
Under the International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea (SOLAS), vessels are required to transmit accurate AIS information.
The Jia Hai Ke 7 is a 70-meter, 2,000-ton vessel built for Zhuhai Jiahai Marine Technology Co. and placed into service in April 2025, according to the PCG.
Tarriela said open-source information describes it as China's first privately owned research vessel equipped with a DP-2 dynamic positioning system and quiet electric propulsion.
These capabilities allow a vessel to maintain its position over a specific point on the seabed, making it suitable for marine geological surveys.
Tarriela said the Chinese vessel has operated alongside seabed-drilling ships.
"The waters off Batanes and the Luzon Strait host critical submarine cable corridors linking the Philippines to Northeast Asia and the wider Indo-Pacific," Tarriela said.

"A seabed-survey vessel hiding its position while holding station in this corridor raises serious concern over the security of the country's undersea communications infrastructure and the potential military use of the data collected," he added.
